newsitem.title: TURKEY: Loading of first tanker for Iraq oil nearly over.
newsitem.headline: Loading of first tanker for Iraq oil nearly over.

text.p: The loading of the first tanker for Iraqi oil at Turkey's Ceyhan terminal was nearly completed, Turkish pipeline officials said on Monday.
An official, who declined to be named, told Reuters the Gole tanker was loaded 153,500 tonnes of Kirkuk crude which will be used by the Turkey's state refiner Tupras.
"The loading operation is about to finish. We are just waiting for the prime minister to come," the official said.

Fatih Sen, regional director of the state pipeline concern Botas, said another tanker of "foreign" origin would arrive at the port, terminus of a twin oil pipeline from Kirkuk, but did not know when it would arrive and from where.

Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will inaugurate a ceremony at 0930 GMT at the Ceyhan port to mark the first loading of Iraqi oil on a tanker in more than six years from the pipeline, unused since the trade embargo on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in August, 1990.
Tupras earlier said it would buy 75,000 barrels per day of Iraqi oil under the U.N.'s oil-for-food deal which allows Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion to buy humanitarian supplies.
